speaker: Head Coach
quote_text:
Good evening, everyone. Hope everyone’s well.  We’re probably not getting around to everyone.  
Raise your hand if you have a question and  we’ll come to you. I’ll look to the front  
row. We’ll come to Sam Dean from The Telegraph.  Well, first of all, what a privilege to play  
the Champions League semi-final in this stadium.  What an energy. What an atmosphere they created.  
We had big parts of the game very similar  to what we wanted. We went ahead with the  
penalty. Unfortunately, in the second half we  started a bit sloppy, with certain giveaways  
and giving them some momentum, and that’s the  moment that they used it. That’s something  
that we knew we had to go through. In the manner  that we gained the penalty, very disappointed.  
In the Premier League it’s not a penalty, but  here I have to accept that, with the rules and  
obviously how consistent they’ve been, for example  yesterday with Bayern Munich, I accept that this  
is a handball. What I am incredibly fuming with is  how the hell the penalty on Ebs gets overturned in  
the manner that happened, when it’s not a clear  and obvious error. This changes the course of the  
game and at this level, I’m sorry, but this cannot  happen. Have you had any explanation on that? Very  
clear explanation. The decision, and then what  happens for a period of time, and the referee  
has to watch it certain times, it’s more clear  than that. I think it’s impossible. And yeah,  
we are all fuming about it. We saw the reaction of  the crowd and the Atlético bench to that moment.  
Do you think that had any impact? There’s nothing  to do with that. I’m sure that they are very, very  
well aware of what the reaction is going to be.  It’s normal, that reaction. We need to apply the  
rules. The same thing that I’m saying that they  applied the rules on Ben White’s penalty. That is  
difficult to accept, but it is a penalty with a  handball. And what they say at the beginning of  
the season, Ebs’ is a clear and very obvious  penalty. That’s it. James, ESPN. Can I ask,  
do you think the process of the use of VAR needs  looking at in general? I don’t know. That’s their  
job and they have a process, and whatever they  do, I’m sure they believe is the right thing.  
I have nothing to say to that. I’m just judging  the action and the manner that happened and the  
way it got overturned. Garmish from Sky. Mikel,  you said you’re fuming. Can you and your players  
now use that as fuel for the rest of the season,  in particular for the second leg? But when you  
have fought so hard for nine months to be in this  position, I mean, that’s another goal that changed  
completely the course of the tie. And it cannot  happen. I’m sorry. We put so much on it. So, so,  
so much on it. This cannot happen. Alex from  BBC. Hi, Mikel. Just on the decision again,  
will you approach UEFA or put a case forward  about this decision not going your way? No,  
no. I leave that to the club to decide what the  best thing to do now is. They’re not going to  
give us the penalty. That’s gone and that’s it.  Let’s talk about football. Tom Reece. Mikel,  
can I ask you about Viktor? Because, you know,  he’s come in for a lot of scrutiny this season,  
but it’s his 19th goal. He had a really strong  first-half performance. Just some reactions to  
his display. Yeah, I agree with that. I think he  had a very strong first half, especially when we  
were more dominant. You know the work he is going  to put in, the situations he created. He created  
the goal and the penalty, and he was ice cold to  score it in the manner that he did. And then the  
second half changed a little bit. Credit to them,  but as well a lot of things that we need to do  
much, much, much better. And I think then we  changed that with the changes. I think the game  
changed as well and we finished on top. Phil  from PA. Sorry, Mikel, just going back to the  
penalty. Do you think that the referee needs to  be a bit stronger? Because obviously he was told  
to go and look at the monitor, but he watched  the replay 12, 13, 14 times and then decided to  
overturn it. I mean, he obviously still had the  power to... I’m not here to judge. The process  
is their process. It’s a decision that is clear.  Okay, stick to it, because that’s the rules. We’ve  
been coaching the players to accept that, and when  there is something different, when you play in the  
semi-final of the Champions League and change it,  it cannot happen. Hi, Mikel. How pleased were you  
with the way your team dealt with this occasion  and this atmosphere? There was obviously pyro  
that was launched at kick-off, grass apparently  was a bit too long, pitch was getting watered at  
half-time. So with all that backdrop, how pleased  are you with the way your team handled it? I’m  
very proud. I said that to the boys. The way we  handle any kind of context for nine and a half  
months is just remarkable. And I really value what  they’ve done because I’ve seen some of the best  
teams in the world here fall apart and concede  three and four, and we didn’t get the result that  
we wanted. The way we planned the game, we wanted  to win it, but at least it’s in our hands, in  
front of our people, to be in that final. And in  a week’s time we’re going to have the opportunity  
to do so. Okay, last two questions from Spanish  media. First, sitting here. Hello, coach. Good  
evening. I would like to ask you again, sorry that  you answered this question in English, about the  
penalty. You said that there’s a consistency in  the Champions League. A handball is a handball,  
but you don’t understand this being reviewed. So  do you not think that in terms of the different  
competitions it’s being called differently?  Well, there were two this time around and  
we’ve seen different criteria. And of course, Ben  White’s handball wouldn’t have been a penalty in  
the Premier League, but it was a handball at UEFA  and we accept this because this is the criterion.  
But then what happened after that, I don’t  understand that. There was a clear contact and  
they took that to the VAR, and they had to review  it 13 times only to overturn the decision. Hello,  
Mikel. Beyond those plays and looking at the game  as a whole, Arsenal were better during the first  
half, but they weren’t creating the chances. Are  you happy with the 1-1 draw, or do you think you  
deserved more, or do you think the result could  have been worse? Well, I think there have been  
many moments. It’s just a privilege and it’s a  great excitement to be playing here. The energy  
is great, the passion and the atmosphere in this  stadium is brilliant. We’ve had times where we  
were superior, where we were better, and we should  have been more clinical and we could have scored  
more goals. We had 15 or 20 minutes during the  second half where they were a bit better, also  
on their merits. And then after the substitutions  we went back to being the team we want to be. So  
again, this decision has changed the course of  the game. But there were also other decisions that  
could have gone the other way. So everything’s to  play for in London. We are putting everything on  
the line on Saturday to win the Premier League,  and then from there on we will start preparing  
for the second leg. Good evening, Mikel. You were  referring to this season. This week we’ve got in  
between before the second leg, you are fighting  for the Premier League and Atlético Madrid are  
facing a less demanding fixture. What’s your  conclusion for tomorrow and how do you face  
the next game? What’s important for you in this  regard? Well, this has been our bread and butter  
during the whole season. Four competitions,  and at the end of today we are in the Champions  
League semi-finals. We are fighting for the  Premier League, so we just need to highlight  
the efforts the players have been putting in.  We’ve seen this. A lot of players are missing,  
are still missing, and we will be fighting on  Saturday and we will be back fighting on Tuesday.
title: Mikel Arteta post-match press conference | Atletico Madrid 1-1 Arsenal | Champions League
